member.name: T:InvisiblePlugin.Commands.CommandReferee
member.summary:
Referee vision: a flagged player (admin or caster) sees invisible players as glow outlines through walls, reusing the wallhack glow system.
Per-viewer render alpha does not exist (m_clrRender is one networked value for all clients), so "seeing" an alpha-0 player is impossible directly — the glow outline is the honest alternative and reads as spectator vision.
Admins are deliberately NOT referees by default: the admin is expected to play the game, and seeing invisible players would be an unfair advantage. Flag yourself with css_ref when you want to observe.

member.name: T:InvisiblePlugin.DyingEntities
member.summary:
Tracks entities we have removed and keeps them out of every viewer's transmit set until the engine has fully processed the removal.
Removal is deferred by the engine (the entity is marked for deletion and freed at the end of the frame); a snapshot sent in the meantime that still carries the entity — or a snapshot that stops carrying it while a client is mid-update — is the classic "missing client entity" / CopyExistingEntity crash window. Each tracked entry stores the entity's raw handle (index + serial), so an entry whose index has been recycled by a NEW entity is dropped and the new entity transmits normally (jRandomSkills EntityManager.recentlyDestroyed pattern).

member.name: F:InvisiblePlugin.DyingEntities.WindowSeconds

member.summary: Call BEFORE removing the entity, while its handle is still readable.

member.name: M:InvisiblePlugin.DyingEntities.SuppressFrom(CounterStrikeSharp.API.Core.CCheckTransmitInfo)
member.summary: Removes every live dying-entity index from the viewer's transmit set. Expired entries and entries whose index was recycled by a different entity are pruned. Allocation-free while the set is empty.

member.name: T:InvisiblePlugin.ForceFullUpdate
member.summary:
Forces a full update (delta tick reset) on all real clients so they re-acquire every entity before transmit hiding starts removing them from snapshots (jRandomSkills ForceFullUpdateToAll pattern).
CounterStrikeSharp 1.0.376 does not expose the network game server, so this vendors a minimal interop (modeled on jRandomSkills CServerSideClient): the engine's NetworkServerService_001 Valve interface, its GetIGameServer vtable slot, the server's client slot vector, and CServerSideClient.m_nDeltaTick. Setting m_nDeltaTick to -1 makes the client's next snapshot a full update.
Offsets come from gamedata/InvisiblePlugin.gamedata.json (shipped alongside the plugin; copy to the server's gamedata directory). A full update resets the client's view angles, so each forced player's angle is restored ~3 ticks later via Teleport with null origin/velocity (angle-only). Not config-gated (standing policy: correctness/robustness ports are always on); any interop failure is logged and skipped — hiding continues to work without it, just without the extra safety margin.

member.name: T:InvisiblePlugin.Logging.DebugLog
member.summary:
Debug logging facade.
Policy (AGENTS.md): configurable, granular, default ON. Every boundary interacting with game state should log its decision so any misbehavior is reconstructible from logs after the fact. Logging only goes quiet when a subsystem has proven itself stable in production (level demoted in config).
Hot-path rules: - Log on CHANGE, not on steady state (e.g. a transmit decision flips, not every tick it stays the same). - Before building an expensive log payload in a hot path, check first; when the channel is gated off the check is the only cost.
Underlying engine is the host's Microsoft.Extensions.Logging + Serilog pipeline (console + daily rotating file, lines tagged with our plugin source context). We add no logging dependencies of our own.

member.name: M:InvisiblePlugin.Modules.Invisible.OnPlayerDeathPre(CounterStrikeSharp.API.Core.EventPlayerDeath,CounterStrikeSharp.API.Core.GameEventInfo)
member.summary: Pre-hook on player_death: the victim's pawn and carried weapons leave the transmit-block state and their render alpha is restored BEFORE the engine processes the death, so this frame's snapshots transmit the pawn again and every client re-acquires it. Membership in InvisiblePlayers intentionally persists: permanent mode re-applies alpha on respawn, reveal mode resets its window on spawn.
